title: JLH (JSON LogHub) Envelope
description: Envelope of every message on the LogHub eventbus. Nine required fields and nothing else at the top level. The payload is a free object whose structure is defined by each type; this schema does not validate payloads.
$comment: loghub-json-schema 1.0.0 (2026-10-03). space follows go-loghub-ident validWorkspace; type follows go-loghub-ident validAgentName. Rules JSON Schema cannot express (uuid precision level 3, level 11-15 usage, step limit processing, timeline semantics, reserved control types) live in the skill text.

uuid.description: Message identity: UUIDv7 (RFC 9562) generated when the envelope is created; never changes when forwarded. Producers use precision level 3 (microseconds in rand_a, nanoseconds in the top 10 bits of rand_b). Any letter case is accepted; producers emit lowercase.

from.description: AgentUUID of the worker that emitted this envelope, persisted across restarts. Any RFC 9562 version (1-8) with the RFC variant, canonical lowercase form. Nil and Max are rejected.

space.description: Workspace (tenant) of the emitting worker; part of the subject loghub.{space}.{type}. Same rule as the go-loghub-ident Workspace.

type.description: Kind of payload, chosen by the program that defines it; selects the payload structure and the subsystem that processes it. Same rule as the go-loghub-ident AgentName. beacon, ping and pong are reserved for the control plane.

level.description: 0-7 severity (emergency..debug); 8 data-signal; 9 data-channel; 10 done-signal; 11-15 reserved (emit only when the type defines the meaning).

sid.description: Session/grouping id (job, workflow, connection). 0 when the type has no session; the process PID by default; never random. Capped at 2^53-1 so every JSON parser reads it exactly.

step.description: Hop counter (anti-loop). 0 on first insertion; +1 on every forward and every derived envelope. A receiver drops and logs an envelope whose step has reached the limit (default 32, can only be lowered).

event.description: When the fact described by the payload happened. uts and sub are the source of truth; iso is the same instant for humans.

uts.description: Unix timestamp, UTC, whole seconds. Upper bound is 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z, the last second iso can represent.

sub.description: Fraction of the second in nanoseconds.

iso.description: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ, UTC, exactly three fraction digits and the Z suffix.

payload.description: Message content. Always a JSON object ({} when empty); its structure is defined by the type.
